audit.name: Sea-crossing raft

prereqAssessment.why: Logs or reed bundles stay together only when lashed; cordage (~50 kya) is the one material precondition of a raft that survives open water.

audit.ageGap: A1 node; prerequisites from A1.

effectsProposed.why: Craft that cross water beyond sight of land put islands and far shores inside the known range (Sahul, ~50 kya).

audit.costConcern: 180 is the cheapest node in the group; fine for an A1 capability with one prerequisite.
audit.rationale: Correct causal prerequisite; the first open-water crossing is an exploration-range capability, not a cargo one.

audit.name: Load-carrying dugout

prereqAssessment.why: Dugouts were hollowed by alternate charring and scraping; controlled fire is the working method (Pesse).
Ground-edge axes and adzes fell and shape the log; both are needed, so AND is right.

audit.ageGap: A1 node; prerequisites from A1.

effectsProposed.why: A load-carrying hull makes river haulage cheaper than carrying along the bank.

audit.rationale: Both atoms are genuine working requirements; river freight is the dugout's causal effect.

audit.name: Sledge

prereqAssessment.why: Runners and crossbars are shaped with ground-stone axes and adzes (Heinola runner).

audit.ageGap: A2 node; prerequisites from A1.

effectsProposed.why: Sledges drag felled logs, quarried stone and winter catches over snow and ice; extractors move more per worker.

audit.rationale: A self-contained hauling capability; the wheel supersedes it for most loads, so a leaf is deliberate.

audit.name: Solid wheel and axle

prereqAssessment.why: The earliest wheeled vehicles (Bronocice, Uruk pictographs) are ox-drawn; the wheel has no use without a draught animal.
Plank wheels and axles were cut with stone woodworking tools (Ljubljana Marshes wheel).

audit.ageGap: A2 node; prerequisites from A1, A2.

effectsProposed.why: A wheeled vehicle carries several times a pack load per animal, so bulk haulage per unit costs less.

audit.costConcern: 3,520 is A3-scale for an A2 node (A2 peers 310-880); it reflects an 8-dependent hub dated at the A2/A3 boundary. Flag for the per-(tree, Age) calibration; no change proposed.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are causal; the wheel is the transport hub of the Bronze Age tree.

audit.name: Ox cart

prereqAssessment.why: The ox cart is the wheel and axle under a load bed; the draught animal comes through wheel_solid.

audit.ageGap: A2 node; prerequisites from A2.

effectsProposed.why: Carts bring harvests and fuel in from fields farther out, so a settlement draws on a wider hinterland.

audit.costConcern: 310 is cheaper than its own prerequisite by an order of magnitude; acceptable for a direct application of the wheel.
audit.rationale: Kept as the vehicle node; its effect (hinterland reach) is distinct from the wheel's (bulk haulage cost).

audit.name: Trackway

prereqAssessment.why: The Sweet Track is split planks pinned with pegs across a marsh: carpentry of the timber-frame tradition.

audit.ageGap: A2 node; prerequisites from A2.
audit.rationale: Live unlock of the path tier (road_track) and, with stone_dry / horse_domestication, of built roads and courier relays. Proposed as a prerequisite of road_paved (see that record), which makes it a bridge rather than a leaf.

audit.name: Square sail

prereqAssessment.why: A hull to carry the mast; OR with raft is right because H3 seagoing craft were reed-bundle boats, not dugouts.
Reed-bundle and raft hulls carried the earliest sails (As-Sabiyah); the OR keeps both lineages.
A sail is woven cloth of sail size; the loom is the material precondition, so AND with the hull group is right.

audit.ageGap: A3 node; prerequisites from A1, A2. Earliest evidence (~5,500 BCE) sits in the A2 window; A3 placement follows the Nile depictions and the spread of sail; not moved (would enlarge the A2 sweep cohort for little gain).

effectsProposed.why: On the Nile the north wind carries boats upstream under sail while the current brings them down: river haulage gets cheaper in both directions.

audit.costConcern: 3,520 fine for the A3 sailing landmark.
audit.rationale: Live unlock of coastal shipping plus the upstream-sailing effect on river haulage.

audit.name: Plank-built boat

prereqAssessment.why: Plank boats grew from extended dugouts (strakes added to a dugout base).
Planks are split, adzed and fitted with copper tools (Khufu ship, Abydos boats).

audit.ageGap: A3 node; prerequisites from A1, A2.
audit.rationale: Live unlock of the harbour (with stone_dry); no operand needed beyond it.

audit.name: Spoked wheel

prereqAssessment.why: The spoked wheel refines the wheel and axle.
Proxy for the bronze chisels and gouges needed to cut mortised hubs and bent felloes; weak but no better tools atom exists.

audit.ageGap: A3 node; prerequisites from A2, A3.

effectsProposed.why: Light spoked wheels make vehicles faster over the same ground.

audit.rationale: Speed is the causal difference from the solid wheel.

audit.name: Engineered paved road

prereqAssessment.why: Engineered roads are laid out on surveyed alignments and grades (Via Appia).

audit.ageGap: A5 node; prerequisites from A3.

effectsProposed.why: All-weather roads were built to move officials, couriers and troops: administrative reach extends further from the capital.

audit.rationale: Add track_road: the road-building craft (causeway, drainage, graded track) is the lineage of the engineered road, and the infrastructure ladder is road_track -> road_built -> road_paved. Without the edge a polity can build paved roads without ever knowing trackways; both atoms are A2/A3, so no sweep or chronology risk.

audit.name: Breast-strap harness

prereqAssessment.why: The harness is for horse traction.
The breast strap is stitched leather; sewing is the material precondition.

audit.ageGap: A5 node; prerequisites from A1, A3.

effectsProposed.why: A breast strap lets a horse pull without choking, so each animal moves heavier loads.

audit.rationale: Prerequisites causal; the effect is load per animal, hence bulk haulage cost.

audit.name: Mathematical cartography

prereqAssessment.why: Ptolemy's maps place places by latitude and longitude derived from geometric astronomy.

audit.ageGap: A5 node; prerequisites from A5.

effectsProposed.why: Coordinate maps let expeditions plan routes to places beyond the explored disc.

audit.rationale: Correct; the effect is the range of planned exploration.

audit.name: Latitude by celestial observation

prereqAssessment.why: Star rising and zenith observations (Babylonian records, Polynesian star compass) give latitude.
Alternative oral sky-knowledge tradition; OR is right because Polynesian wayfinding did not depend on written records.

audit.ageGap: A4 node; prerequisites from A2, A4.

effectsProposed.why: Holding a latitude out of sight of land lets each expedition push further.

audit.rationale: OR between two independent star-knowledge traditions is correct; astronomy_records is dated after the node but is not must-held.

audit.name: Monsoon navigation

prereqAssessment.why: Running before the seasonal wind needs sail.
The monsoon calendar (when to sail out and back) is kept by sky observation.

audit.ageGap: A5 node; prerequisites from A3, A4.

effectsProposed.why: Regular annual crossings between India, Arabia and East Africa link distant markets so prices converge faster.

audit.rationale: Correct; effect is market integration across the ocean basin.

audit.name: Lateen sail

prereqAssessment.why: The lateen is a rig variant; sailing practice comes first.

audit.ageGap: A5 node; prerequisites from A3.

effectsProposed.why: Ships that can sail closer to the wind wait less in port for a fair wind, so cargoes reach market sooner.

audit.rationale: Correct; effect differs from its A5 lane neighbours (exploration range, market integration).

audit.name: Mortise-and-tenon hull

prereqAssessment.why: Edge-joined mortise-and-tenon planking is a plank-boat construction method.

audit.ageGap: A3 node; prerequisites from A3.

effectsProposed.why: Locked plank seams allow large cargo hulls (Uluburun carried ~10 t of copper), lowering cost per unit carried.

audit.rationale: Correct; large seagoing cargo hulls.

audit.name: Nailed horseshoe
audit.ageGap: A6 node; prerequisites from A3, A4.

effectsProposed.why: Shod horses keep pace on hard and wet ground without going lame.

audit.rationale: Correct; a terminal practical improvement; sprung_coach (new) now builds on it.

audit.name: Magnetic compass

prereqAssessment.why: A magnetised iron needle needs iron; lodestone knowledge is implicit.

audit.ageGap: A6 node; prerequisites from A4.

effectsProposed.why: Holding a course under overcast skies lets each voyage of exploration reach further.

audit.rationale: Correct; landmark-scale delta because exploreStepNodes is an integer of base 3 and moves only when Σ crosses 0.34.

audit.name: Stern-post rudder

prereqAssessment.why: Redundant: mortise_hull itself requires plank_boat, so the OR reduces to plank_boat. Harmless.
The stern-post rudder hangs on a plank hull; Han river boats had no mortise-and-tenon shell.

audit.ageGap: A6 node; prerequisites from A3. Earliest evidence ~100 CE lies in the A5 window; A6 placement follows the European adoption (~1,180); kept.

effectsProposed.why: The rudder appears first on Chinese river craft (~100 CE): larger boats can be steered on rivers, cheapening river haulage.

audit.rationale: OR is redundant but not wrong; no change.

audit.name: Watertight bulkheads

prereqAssessment.why: Weak causally (bulkheads are a hull technique), but it carries the Chinese junk lineage and keeps ocean_junk requiring a rudder; replacing it would need a compensating edge.

audit.ageGap: A6 node; prerequisites from A6.

effectsProposed.why: A holed compartment no longer sinks the ship: fewer cargoes are lost on the way, so stocks reach markets.

audit.rationale: Kept as is; the prerequisite is weak but chain-preserving.

audit.name: Portolan chart

prereqAssessment.why: Portolan rhumb lines are compass bearings.

audit.ageGap: A6 node; prerequisites from A5, A6.

effectsProposed.why: Accurate coastal charts extend how far exploration can be planned.

audit.rationale: Correct; differs from compass (step) by acting on range.

audit.name: Cog

prereqAssessment.why: The cog is the first northern ship with a stern rudder.

audit.ageGap: A6 node; prerequisites from A3, A6.

effectsProposed.why: The flat-bottomed, high-sided cog carried Baltic grain, timber and herring in bulk at low cost.

audit.rationale: Correct; bulk carrier of the Hanseatic trade.

audit.name: Caravel

prereqAssessment.why: Lateen rig lets the caravel beat home against the trades.
Required for a seagoing hull of this size.

audit.ageGap: A7 node; prerequisites from A5, A6.

effectsProposed.why: Landmark exploration ship: each expedition reaches much further along unknown coasts.

audit.costConcern: 16,730 is 2.8x the carrack (5,910) although the caravel is the smaller ship; it carries the a7_ocean milestone. Flag for calibration.
audit.rationale: Correct prerequisites; live ocean_shipping unlock plus landmark exploration step.

audit.name: Carrack and full-rigged ship

prereqAssessment.why: The carrack takes the cog's rig and rudder onto a frame-first hull.

audit.ageGap: A7 node; prerequisites from A5, A6.

effectsProposed.why: Large frame-first hulls carry far more cargo per crew member.

audit.rationale: Correct; live unlocks plus bulk capacity.

audit.name: Polynesian voyaging canoe

prereqAssessment.why: Voyaging hulls are dugout bases with sewn strakes.

audit.ageGap: A6 node; prerequisites from A1, A4. Lapita voyaging (~1,500 BCE) is older; A6 placement follows the East Polynesian settlement era (~1,000 CE); kept.

effectsProposed.why: Double-hulled canoes carried whole founding parties with crops and animals to new islands.

audit.rationale: Correct; the effect is founding-party size, unique in the lane.

audit.name: Celestial navigation with instruments

prereqAssessment.why: Mariner's astrolabe and quadrant measure altitude at sea.
Declination tables and reduction of sights.

audit.ageGap: A7 node; prerequisites from A6.

effectsProposed.why: Fixing latitude at sea with instruments extends the range of open-ocean exploration.

audit.rationale: Correct.

audit.name: Longitude by chronometer

prereqAssessment.why: Longitude by chronometer completes the celestial fix.
Harrison's H4 used a verge escapement.

audit.ageGap: A7 node; prerequisites from A6, A7.

effectsProposed.why: Known longitude shortens passages and cuts wrecks: ocean trade connects markets more reliably.

audit.rationale: Correct; a terminal navigation achievement.

audit.name: Mercator projection

prereqAssessment.why: The projection is a trigonometric construction.

audit.ageGap: A7 node; prerequisites from A5, A6.

effectsProposed.why: Straight-course ocean charts made long planned passages routine, including emigrant voyages: people move further.

audit.rationale: Kept; overlaps portolan and celestial_navigation in capability, so the effect is deliberately placed on a different operand.

audit.name: Steam locomotive

prereqAssessment.why: Trevithick's high-pressure engine made a self-propelled engine light enough.

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A8.

effectsProposed.why: The first locomotives (Penydarren 1804, colliery lines) hauled coal and ore from pits.

audit.rationale: Correct.

audit.name: Railway network
audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A3, A8.

effectsProposed.why: Landmark: rail freight cut overland bulk haulage cost several-fold.
Stations bring distant farms within a city's supply range.

audit.rationale: Correct; live unlock plus landmark freight effect.

audit.name: Steamboat

prereqAssessment.why: Imprecise (19th-century hulls are frame-first, not mortise-and-tenon), but it only stands for 'a wooden hull' and is long complete under the A8 sweep; no change.

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A3, A8.

effectsProposed.why: Landmark: steamboats run upstream against any current, transforming river freight.

audit.rationale: Kept; the hull atom is a weak proxy with no reachability consequence.

audit.name: Screw propeller

prereqAssessment.why: Smith's and Ericsson's propellers were explicitly Archimedean screws.

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A5, A8.

effectsProposed.why: Screw steamers keep schedules at sea regardless of wind: distant markets integrate faster.

audit.rationale: Correct; unit.ironclad is not live yet (M7/M8). Deferred (not live): unit.ironclad.

audit.name: Iron hull

prereqAssessment.why: Iron hulls first went to sea as steamers (Aaron Manby).

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A8.

effectsProposed.why: Iron hulls allowed ships far larger than timber could, cutting cost per tonne carried.

audit.rationale: Correct; unit.ironclad deferred. Deferred (not live): unit.ironclad.

audit.name: Macadam road

prereqAssessment.why: Macadam is a cheaper engineered road surface built on the road-engineering tradition.

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A5.

effectsProposed.why: Compacted broken stone without massive foundations makes road building cheaper.

audit.rationale: Correct; live unlock plus build-cost effect.

audit.name: Safety bicycle
audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A4, A8.

effectsProposed.why: Cheap personal transport widened rural labour and marriage markets: people move more readily.

audit.rationale: Correct.

audit.name: Powered heavier-than-air flight

prereqAssessment.why: Lift data and three-axis control (Wright gliders).

audit.ageGap: A9 node; prerequisites from A8. 1903 lies in the A8 window; A9 placement follows aviation's impact from 1914; kept.

effectsProposed.why: Landmark: aerial reconnaissance; formation sight is an integer of base 1, so only a landmark delta changes it.

audit.rationale: Correct; live airfield plus aerial reconnaissance. Deferred (not live): unit.aircraft_carrier, unit.military_aircraft.

audit.name: All-metal monoplane
audit.ageGap: A9 node; prerequisites from A9.

effectsProposed.why: Long-range all-metal aircraft survey remote country: each expedition covers more ground.

audit.rationale: Correct.

audit.name: Mass-produced automobile
audit.ageGap: A9 node; prerequisites from A8. 1913 sits at the A8/A9 boundary; kept.

effectsProposed.why: Motor trucks and cars bring a far wider rural area into each town's supply range.

audit.rationale: Correct.

audit.name: Liquid-fuel rocket

prereqAssessment.why: Proxy for fuel-combustion engineering; a liquid-oxygen atom (refrigeration, Linde air liquefaction) would be more specific - noted, not changed.

audit.ageGap: A9 node; prerequisites from A7, A8, A9.
audit.costConcern: 378,470 is 2x its own dependent orbital_launch_vehicle (189,240) and 5.7x aircraft; a 1926 sounding rocket should not outcost the 1957 orbital launcher.
audit.rationale: Cost inversion against its dependent; propose recalibrating to the A9 aircraft band (~66,900) at the integration step. Live spaceport unlock is its effect. Deferred (not live): project.orbital_launch, unit.missile.

audit.name: Container shipping

prereqAssessment.why: Steel cellular hulls descend from iron hulls.

audit.ageGap: A9 node; prerequisites from A8, A9.

effectsProposed.why: Landmark: standard boxes cut port handling cost and time by an order of magnitude.

audit.rationale: Correct.

audit.name: Electric railway and metro
audit.ageGap: A9 node; prerequisites from A8. Dated 1890 but placed A9; proposed move to A8.

effectsProposed.why: Trams and metros let workers reach factory, office and shop jobs across a whole city, so larger specialist classes can form.

audit.costConcern: 47,310 is high if moved to A8 (A8 transport peers 8,360-23,650); recalibrate with the move.
audit.rationale: Emerged 1890 (City and South London Railway) and the electric tram boom of 1888-1910 lie squarely in the A8 window; both prerequisites are A8 and its only dependent (high_speed_rail) is A9, so moving it to A8 breaks no edge.

audit.name: Satellite navigation

audit.ageGap: A9 node; prerequisites from A9.

effectsProposed.why: Satellite-tracked fleets and routing speed goods from store to market.

audit.name: Crewed spaceflight

effectsProposed.why: Biotelemetry built to monitor astronauts passed into hospital patient monitoring.

audit.name: Space station

effectsProposed.why: A permanent shared microgravity laboratory lowers the cost of experiments for research institutions.

audit.rationale: Correct.

audit.ageGap: A9 node; prerequisites from A9.

effectsProposed.why: Cheap launch fills orbit with imaging constellations that map remote ground.

audit.rationale: Correct.

audit.name: Earth observation
audit.ageGap: A9 node; prerequisites from A8, A9.

effectsProposed.why: Landsat imagery maps terrain beyond any ground expedition's reach.

audit.rationale: Correct prerequisites; lane 'naval' is a misfit (it is remote sensing), reported as a finding, no lane change proposed.

audit.name: High-speed rail
audit.ageGap: A9 node; prerequisites from A8, A9.

effectsProposed.why: Three-hour journeys over 500 km let people move and commute much further.

audit.rationale: Correct.

audit.name: Jet airliner
audit.ageGap: A9 node; prerequisites from A9.

effectsProposed.why: Air freight and business travel tie distant markets together.

effectsProposed.why: Helicopter airlift reaches cut-off districts with relief food.

audit.ageGap: A9 node; prerequisites from A9.

effectsProposed.why: Speculative: fast fusion transit makes off-world ore runs worthwhile.

audit.ageGap: A9 node; prerequisites from A9.

effectsProposed.why: Per level: cheaper launch thickens communications constellations that reach remote districts.

audit.rationale: Repeatable; operand proposed as its per-level effect (convert to gapFraction under contract §4).

audit.ageGap: A9 node; prerequisites from A8, A9.

newNodes.name: Desert caravan
newNodes.emerged: ~1,000 BCE South Arabian incense caravans on the dromedary; ~300 CE trans-Saharan camel caravans
newNodes.prereqRationale: The dromedary (camel, ~1,000 BCE; Bactrian ~2,500 BCE) is the carrier that can go days without water; organised caravans presuppose exchange between communities at a counted standard (trade, ~3,500 BCE). Both A3 and older than the node.
newNodes.desc: Strings of camels, with wells, guides and halting places, carry goods across deserts that no cart or donkey could cross, so towns far apart can trade overland.
newNodes.distinctFrom: trade (A3) is exchange between settlements within ordinary route range by any carrier; this is the specific ability to cross waterless country, lengthening the longest viable overland route rather than cheapening haulage.

newNodes.name: Sprung coach and stage service
newNodes.emerged: ~1,450 CE Kocs coach (Hungary); ~1,610 CE first scheduled stagecoach services; ~1,665 CE steel-spring suspension
newNodes.prereqRationale: A light passenger vehicle on spoked wheels (wheel_spoked) drawn by shod teams changed at stages (horseshoe, ~900 CE); steel leaf springs need carburized steel (steel_carburized). All three are dated before ~1,450 CE.
newNodes.desc: Coaches hung on straps and later steel springs, drawn by fresh teams changed at regular stages, carry passengers, mail and light goods on timetabled runs between towns.
newNodes.distinctFrom: horseshoe (A6) protects the animal and macadam (A8) improves the surface; this is the vehicle and staging system, the only A7 overland transport node (the A7 transport lane is otherwise empty).

findings: Lane coverage: transport has no A4 and no A7 node (A7 is entirely naval); the two new nodes (camel_caravan A4, sprung_coach A7) fill those overland gaps without duplicating trade or horseshoe.

A9 transport is crowded (19 nodes, 8 of them space nodes) and the registry has no space operands; space nodes carry spin-off effects (medicine, research, civics, universities) at the minimum delta. A space-programme operand would let them act causally.

Integer fog operands: formationSightNodes (base 1) moves only when Σ reaches 1.0 and exploreStepNodes (base 3) only at Σ 0.34; balloon and aircraft carry landmark 0.5 for sight, compass/caravel 0.08/0.12 for step. Small deltas on these operands are inert until summed past a threshold.
Cost inversion: rocket (378,470) costs 2x its dependent orbital_launch_vehicle (189,240); caravel (16,730) costs 2.8x the larger carrack (5,910); wheel_solid (3,520) is A3-scale inside A2.

Age placements: electric_traction (1890) is proposed for A8; aircraft (1903) and automobile_mass (1913) also predate 1914 but are kept in A9 for impact. sail_square (~5,500 BCE evidence) and stern_rudder (~100 CE) sit one Age later than their earliest dates; kept.
Redundant OR/AND atoms (stern_rudder's mortise_hull, cog's plank_boat, mercator's cartography, motor_road's petroleum_refining) are harmless and left as written.
earth_observation and gps sit in the naval lane; they are remote sensing and positioning, a lane misfit with no gameplay consequence.
Four nodes unlock activity.ocean_shipping by OR (caravel, carrack, polynesian_canoe, ocean_junk); only the first completed one matters, so each also carries its own operand effect.

trade.costPerBulkCostUnit receives 0.30 from this group (wheel_solid, collar_harness, mortise_hull, cog, carrack, iron_hull, railway, container_shipping) against a cap of 0.8, on top of 0.27 from T1-T3: the integrator should watch this cap.
Civ VI space-race projects and route types are not in the supplied data (no Projects or Routes table); crewed_spaceflight and lunar_flight are marked not-reviewed for Civ VI.
